claims.statement: The ESPR creates an interoperable digital-product-passport framework with persistent identifiers, data carriers, access rights, portability, and customer-personal-data restrictions, but product-group delegated acts determine which products, data, actors, and dates apply.

From 18 February 2027, each industrial battery above 2 kWh placed on the EU market or put into service must have a battery passport, creating a near-term standards-adjacent wedge for residential storage without making the installer the statutory economic operator.
Poland had 1,636,673 grid-connected RES micro-installations at the end of 2025 and 99.9% were photovoltaic, providing a large installed service base rather than proof of passport demand.

The EU solar fleet reached 406 GW in 2025 while the residential share of new installations fell from 28% in 2023 to 14% in 2025, supporting an aftermarket focus but warning against relying only on new-install flow.

Installer platforms already generate handover packs, commissioning records, customer portals, service workflows, and QR-linked documentation, so a passport can be bundled as a feature and must win on portability and aftermarket outcomes.
A direct battery-DPP vendor publishes plans from EUR149 per month including 1,000 annual passports and extra-passport pricing from EUR0.20, imposing price pressure on a compliance-only passport.

EU database law can prohibit unauthorised extraction or reuse of substantial database contents, so manufacturer compatibility data must be licensed, supplied by users, or built from lawful individual observations rather than scraped wholesale.

Hypothesis: a portable installer-created service record can bridge manufacturer portals and make repair easier, but the reviewed law and manufacturer workflow do not establish owner or third-party rights to copy manuals, diagnostics, or compatibility tables into a commercial registry.

contrary_evidence: ESPR is a framework whose delegated acts define product-specific obligations; it does not make every current solar inverter or heat pump require a statutory DPP today.

The right-to-repair directive applies to goods listed through product-specific reparability rules and creates a public European repair platform, so it does not grant an immediate exclusive directory opportunity.
SolarPlus, InsTool, and Payaca already generate handover packs and customer documentation, and manufacturer portals such as SolarEdge already bind sites and serials to installer accounts.
Collecta DPP publishes low per-passport pricing, making 20-60 PLN per simple compliance record difficult to defend without service or transaction value.
EU database rights and copyright in technical materials constrain bulk reuse; no reviewed source establishes licences to republish manufacturer manuals, diagnostic codes, or part-compatibility data.
The EU residential new-install share fell sharply by 2025, so a growth model based only on new QR labels is fragile.

economics.acquisition_route: Use the family company only to instrument actual battery and inverter service cases and give owners free records; measure issue-intake completion, callbacks, resolution, and completed paid work. Recruit external service providers through wholesalers or service networks only after case flow exists. The family pilot is not evidence of outside demand or paid conversion.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Unvalidated years 8-12 arithmetic requirement, not a forecast: retaining the prior 1600 PLN average transaction, 8% fee, 20% EBITDA margin, 5x EBITDA multiple, and 70% founder ownership assumptions, about 55804 completed annual transactions would produce about 7.14 million PLN revenue, 1.43 million PLN EBITDA, and 5 million PLN founder equity. The prior 25000-transaction case alone produces 3.2 million PLN revenue and about 2.24 million PLN founder equity, so removing assumed installer subscription and authorised-data revenue exposes service volume as the binding scale condition. Transaction volume, basket, take rate, margin, multiple, ownership, and timing remain unvalidated.
economics.founder_time: 12-18 hours weekly for the free record, consented issue intake, and a closed family-company service-case test. External dispatch, provider onboarding, owner support, verification, and disputes must be delegated before expansion beyond a bounded network.
economics.gross_margin_basis: The basic record is a zero-price acquisition and context layer rather than 80-90% gross-margin software revenue. Gross margin equals verified completion-fee revenue less payment costs, technician verification, owner and provider support, insurance, refunds, and disputes; it is unknown and likely more operationally sensitive than registry software margin.
economics.payback: Unknown. A provider should pay only after a completed job and only when job gross profit exceeds the outcome fee; any subscription must wait for evidence that measured administrative savings repay it within 12 months. Each completed case must also cover the founder-side variable orchestration cost.
economics.pricing: Validation structure, not proven pricing: 0 PLN for the basic owner-controlled record and no per-asset creation fee; retain the existing 6-10% hypothesis only on verified completed service or parts transactions. A 99-399 PLN monthly provider workflow subscription remains optional and must not launch until measured savings support it.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Repeat value comes from append-only service events and completed resolutions rather than record creation. Owners can reuse the asset identity across faults, service, and transfer; providers repeat only if cases convert profitably. Both behaviours remain unknown.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Lawfully collected installed configuration, service, failure, and verified transaction history tied to persistent asset identities
fingerprint.customer: Polish battery and inverter service firms handling fault, warranty, transfer, or orphaned-equipment cases; equipment owners use the portable record free
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Instrument family-company service cases first, distribute free records through installer handovers and owner service interactions, then recruit fulfilment providers through wholesalers and service networks only after case flow is measured
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Free owner-controlled QR asset and service record plus technician-reviewed issue intake and service or parts routing, funded by an outcome fee on completed jobs; any provider subscription is gated on measured workflow savings
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: A service or parts provider pays only when an owner-authorised, technician-reviewed case becomes a verified completed paid job; basic record creation is free
fingerprint.problem_trigger: An owner reports a battery or inverter fault, lacks usable service context, changes ownership, or needs a technician-approved replacement or repair

founder_fit: The family renewable installer provides bounded access to real handovers and service cases for testing the free record and case workflow without claiming that unrelated providers will adopt or pay.

The founder's data and automation skills fit consented document extraction, asset identity, issue intake, and workflow analytics, while technicians retain every safety-sensitive diagnosis and compatibility decision.

A free record plus closed family-company service-case pilot can fit 12-18 hours weekly and available capital; open routing, provider onboarding, and dispute handling remain gated on measured case economics and delegation.
The model is low-camera and system-oriented, but provider recruitment and delegated service operations still require bounded B2B selling and operational oversight.
risks: Incorrect compatibility or diagnostic routing can damage equipment, void warranties, or create electrical and fire hazards even when a technician approves the final decision.
A record containing address, ownership, serials, photos, faults, and system topology creates privacy and physical-security exposure.
Manufacturers or installer platforms can restrict data access, bundle service intake, or keep cases inside their own networks.
Outcome-paid orchestration can become support-heavy and require provider verification, dispute handling, refunds, insurance, and delegated operations before sufficient case volume.
Free records may attract owners without producing provider-acceptable or completed paid service cases.
A privately issued service record can be confused with the statutory EU product or battery passport unless naming and responsibility remain explicit.

structure.commercial_archetype: Free asset registry feeding an outcome-paid, technician-verified service orchestration network
structure.control_point: The portable owner-authorised equipment identity plus accumulated consented service-case and completion history
structure.critical_dependency: Enough recurring owner-consented cases and technician-verified fulfilment for completion fees to cover acquisition, verification, support, insurance, and disputes without unlicensed manufacturer data

thesis: Keep the owner-authorised portable equipment identity, but stop selling passport creation. Give owners and originating installers the basic QR asset and service record free, then use owner-consented records to assemble battery and inverter fault cases for technician review and provider acceptance. Monetise only verified completed service or parts transactions; launch an optional provider workflow subscription only after measured administrative savings. The record becomes acquisition and service-context infrastructure rather than the paid product, while all safety-sensitive routing stays human-approved and all manufacturer material remains linked, licensed, user-supplied, or lawfully observed.
title: Free Renewable Equipment Service Record and Outcome-Paid Resolution
uncertainties: Which initial category produces enough completed service cases: residential batteries or inverters.
Whether owners activate, consent to, maintain, and transfer a free portable record.
Whether enough owner-authorised faults become verified completed paid jobs to support a 6-10% outcome-fee hypothesis.
Whether service and parts providers accept outcome-based payment and repeat after accounting for lead quality, travel, parts, and support.
Which manufacturer documents, identifiers, diagnostics, and compatibility attributes can be stored, linked, licensed, or lawfully observed.
Actual technician-verification, insurance, privacy, payment, refund, and dispute costs per completed case.
Whether statutory battery passports and manufacturer portals expose interoperable data that the owner-authorised service record may lawfully reference.
Whether the free record produces enough case flow without a broader installer CRM or paid acquisition channel.
